intro_text.en: Unit 2 of Engineering Materials Science: what a phase is and how the phase rule counts them, what a cooling curve tells a foundry, how a casting freezes from the mould wall inwards and why that leaves three zones of grains, how a solid solution differs from a compound, and how to read the three diagrams that the rest of the subject stands on - copper-nickel, lead-tin and iron-carbon. The lever rule is worked on every one of them, the eutectoid of steel is computed for three carbon contents, and six solved numericals follow in section 2.7.

Lever rule ત્રણેય પર ગણાયેલો છે, સ્ટીલના eutectoid ની ગણતરી ત્રણ carbon content માટે કરેલી છે, અને પછી વિભાગ 2.7 માં છ ઉકેલેલા દાખલા છે.

title.en: 2.1 Phase, component and the phase rule

h.en: Phase, component and degrees of freedom
h.gu: Phase, component અને degrees of freedom

body.en:
A phase is a part of the material that is the same everywhere in it: same crystal structure, same composition, and a boundary you could draw round it. Ice and water in one glass are two phases; a Cu-Ni solid solution is one phase however much nickel it holds. A component is the smallest set of chemical species needed to describe every phase present, and the degrees of freedom tell you how many of the variables (temperature, pressure, composition) you may change without losing a phase.

Gibbs phase rule: F = C - P + 2 every diagram in this subject is drawn at 1 atmosphere, so the pressure is fixed: condensed phase rule: F = C - P + 1 pure iron, 1450 C (austenite only): C=1 P=1 -> F = 1-1+1 = 1 pure iron at 1538 C (solid + liquid): C=1 P=2 -> F = 1-2+1 = 0 Pb-Sn eutectic, 183 C (L + alpha + beta): C=2 P=3 -> F = 2-3+1 = 0 40 % Sn at 200 C (alpha + liquid): C=2 P=2 -> F = 2-2+1 = 1

Why it is true. F = 0 means the point is invariant: the eutectic of lead-tin freezes at one temperature and one composition and you cannot move either without losing a phase. F = 1 means you may pick the temperature and the compositions then follow the two boundaries of the field - which is exactly what a tie line does.

કોઈ સામગ્રીનો જે ભાગ બધે એકસરખો હોય તે phase છે: એક જ crystal structure, એક જ composition, અને તેની આસપાસ સીમા દોરી શકાય. એક ગ્લાસમાં ice અને water બે phase છે; Cu-Ni solid solution માં nickel ગમે તેટલું હોય તો પણ તે એક જ phase છે. Component એ હાજર બધા phase વર્ણવવા માટે જરૂરી લઘુતમ chemical species છે, અને degrees of freedom કહે છે કે phase ગુમાવ્યા વગર તમે temperature, pressure અને composition માંથી કેટલા બદલી શકો.

h.en: Cooling curves: what a foundryman reads off them
h.gu: Cooling curves: ફાઉન્ડ્રીવાળો તેમાંથી શું વાંચે છે

body.en:
Pour a metal into a mould, put a thermocouple in it and plot temperature against time. A pure metal cools in a straight line until it reaches its freezing point, then the curve goes flat: the latent heat of fusion is coming out as fast as the mould takes heat away, so the temperature does not fall until every atom has solidified. An alloy freezes over a range - the liquidus where the first solid appears and the solidus where the last liquid goes - so the curve only changes slope, and the slushy band in between is the mushy zone.

latent heat released in time dt: dQ = m Lf held flat while the mould removes heat at q W: t_arrest = m Lf / q example: 2 kg of iron, Lf = 247 kJ/kg, mould takes 500 W t_arrest = 2 x 247000 / 500 = 988 s = 16.5 min of flat curve alloy freezing range = T_liquidus - T_solidus the 70/30 alloy of figure: 1500 - 1380 = 120 C of mushy zone

Why it is true. The flat part is the melting point measured from outside; the length of the flat part is the latent heat divided by the rate at which the mould removes heat. That is why a thin casting freezes quickly and a heavy section keeps its heat - and why the heavy section is the one that ends up with shrinkage porosity.

Common mistake. A small dip below the freezing point before the flat part is undercooling, not a lower melting point: the metal has to be pushed below its freezing point before nuclei form, and the temperature then jumps back up as they grow (recalescence). Read the flat part, not the dip.
body.gu:
Mould માં ધાતુ રેડો, તેમાં thermocouple નાખો અને time સામે temperature દોરો. Pure metal ગલનબિંદુ સુધી સીધી રેખામાં ઠંડું થાય, પછી રેખા સપાટ થઈ જાય: latent heat of fusion એટલી ઝડપથી બહાર નીકળે છે જેટલી ઝડપથી mould ગરમી લે છે, તેથી બધું ઘન ન થાય ત્યાં સુધી temperature ઘટતું નથી. Alloy એક range માં થીજે છે - liquidus જ્યાં પ્રથમ ઘન દેખાય અને solidus જ્યાં છેલ્લું પ્રવાહી જાય - તેથી રેખા ફક્ત ઢાળ બદલે છે, અને વચ્ચેનો લપટાવાળો પટ્ટો mushy zone છે.

latent heat released in time dt: dQ = m Lf held flat while the mould removes heat at q W: t_arrest = m Lf / q example: 2 kg of iron, Lf = 247 kJ/kg, mould takes 500 W t_arrest = 2 x 247000 / 500 = 988 s = 16.5 min of flat curve alloy freezing range = T_liquidus - T_solidus the 70/30 alloy of figure: 1500 - 1380 = 120 C of mushy zone

કેમ સાચું છે. સપાટ ભાગ એ બહારથી માપેલું ગલનબિંદુ છે; સપાટ ભાગની લંબાઈ એ latent heat ભાગ્યા mould ગરમી લે તેવા દર જેટલી છે. તેથી પાતળું casting જલદી થીજે છે અને જાડો ભાગ ગરમી રાખે છે - અને તેથી જ જાડા ભાગમાં shrinkage porosity રહી જાય છે.

સામાન્ય ભૂલ. સપાટ ભાગ પહેલાં ગલનબિંદુથી થોડું નીચે જવું તે undercooling છે, ગલનબિંદુ નીચું થયું નથી: nuclei બનતા પહેલાં ધાતુને તેના ગલનબિંદુથી નીચે ધકેલવી પડે છે, અને પછી nuclei વધતાં temperature પાછું ઉપર કૂદે છે (recalescence). સપાટ ભાગ વાંચો, ખાડો નહીં.

h.en: Nucleation, dendrites and the three zones of an ingot
h.gu: Nucleation, dendrites અને ingot ના ત્રણ zone

body.en:
Solidification needs somewhere to start. Homogeneous nucleation is a cluster of atoms forming on its own in the melt; it needs a large undercooling because the new surface costs energy. Heterogeneous nucleation uses a ready-made surface - the mould wall, an oxide skin, or a deliberately added particle - and needs only a small undercooling, so it is what actually happens in a foundry. Once a nucleus exists it grows fastest along the directions where it can reject its latent heat, which gives the tree-shaped dendrite; the arms of neighbouring dendrites meet and leave a grain boundary.

critical radius of a nucleus: r* = 2 gamma Tm / (L dT) energy barrier: dG* = 16 pi gamma^3 Tm^2 / (3 L^2 dT^2) iron: gamma = 0.2 J/m2, Tm = 1811 K, L = 1.9e9 J/m3, dT = 100 K r* = 2 x 0.2 x 1811 / (1.9e9 x 100) = 3.8e-9 m = 3.8 nm dT = 200 K -> r* = 1.9 nm: double the undercooling, half the nucleus
ZoneWhere it freezesGrainsWhy
Chill zoneagainst the mould wallfine, equiaxedwall nucleates many grains at once
Columnar zonenext to it, growing inwardslong, parallelheat leaves through the wall, so they grow that way
Equiaxed centrelast, in the hot middlecoarse, randomslow cooling, few nuclei left

Common mistake. The three zones are not always there. A thin section or a well-inoculated alloy may be all equiaxed, and a pure metal poured into a cold metal mould may be almost all columnar. The zones are a description of the heat flow, not a rule.

ઘન થવા માટે શરૂઆતનું સ્થળ જોઈએ. Homogeneous nucleation એ પ્રવાહીમાં પોતાની જાતે બનતું atoms નું ટોળું છે; નવી surface ઊર્જા માંગે છે તેથી તેને ઘણું undercooling જોઈએ. Heterogeneous nucleation તૈયાર surface વાપરે છે - mould ની દીવાલ, oxide નો પડ, કે જાણીને ઉમેરેલો કણ - અને થોડું જ undercooling માંગે છે, તેથી ફાઉન્ડ્રીમાં ખરેખર એ જ બને છે. Nucleus બન્યા પછી જ્યાં latent heat સહેલાઈથી નીકળે તે દિશામાં તે સૌથી ઝડપથી વધે છે, જેનાથી ઝાડ જેવું dendrite બને છે; પાડોશી dendrite ના ડાળા મળે ત્યાં grain boundary રહી જાય છે.

h.en: Casting defects that come from solidification

body.en:
Almost every casting defect is a consequence of one fact: the metal shrinks when it freezes, and it freezes from the outside in. The last liquid is trapped somewhere inside, and when it finally freezes there is nothing left to fill the hole it leaves. A shrinkage cavity (pipe) forms where the feeder could not reach, porosity where gas or shrinkage is spread out as small holes, segregation where alloying elements are pushed ahead of the growing dendrites, and hot tears where a contracting skin is pulled apart while it is still weak.

h.en: Grain size sets the strength: Hall-Petch
h.gu: Grain size તાકાત નક્કી કરે: Hall-Petch

body.en:
A dislocation gliding along its slip plane stops at a grain boundary, because the next grain has its lattice at a different angle. The pile-up of dislocations at the boundary raises the stress there until the neighbouring grain yields too. Make the grains smaller and there are more boundaries, so the pile-ups are shorter and a larger stress is needed to push the slip across: this is the Hall-Petch relation. It is the one strengthening method that also raises toughness, which is why normalising and grain refining are so common.

sigma_y = sigma_0 + k d^(-1/2) sigma_0 = 100 MPa, k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5 d = 0.0625 mm -> d^-1/2 = 4.00 -> sigma_y = 100 + 93.6 = 194 MPa d = 0.0156 mm -> d^-1/2 = 8.00 -> sigma_y = 100 + 187.2 = 287 MPa half the grain size, + 93 MPa on the yield strength
ASTM grain size number: n = 2^(N-1) grains per square inch at 100x N = 6 -> n = 32 -> d = 25.4/(100 x sqrt(32)) = 0.045 mm N = 10 -> n = 512 -> d = 25.4/(100 x sqrt(512)) = 0.011 mm

Check your answer. The relation is a straight line only when plotted against d^(-1/2). Plot against d itself and it curves, which is exactly what a student loses marks for.

Slip plane પર સરતું dislocation grain boundary પર અટકે છે, કારણ કે પછીના grain નું lattice જુદા ખૂણે છે. Boundary પર dislocations નું થતું ઢગલો ત્યાં stress વધારે છે જ્યાં સુધી પાડોશી grain પણ yield ન થાય. Grains નાના કરો તો boundaries વધે, ઢગલા ટૂંકા રહે અને slip પસાર કરવા મોટું stress જોઈએ: આ Hall-Petch સંબંધ છે. તાકાત વધારવાની આ એક જ રીત છે જે toughness પણ વધારે છે, તેથી normalising અને grain refining ખૂબ વપરાય છે.

title.en: 2.3 Solid solution, intermediate phase and the Hume-Rothery rules
title.gu: 2.3 Solid solution, intermediate phase અને Hume-Rothery rules

h.en: Two ways to dissolve one metal in another
h.gu: એક ધાતુ બીજીમાં ઓગળવાની બે રીત

body.en:
A solid solution is a single crystal in which one kind of atom has been replaced by another without changing the lattice. If the two atoms are of similar size the substitute atom simply takes the place of the one it replaced: a substitutional solution, as in copper-nickel, brass or stainless steel. If the second atom is much smaller it cannot take a lattice site and instead sits in the gap between the atoms: an interstitial solution, as carbon, nitrogen or hydrogen in iron. Interstitial atoms are few - carbon reaches only 2.14 % in austenite and 0.02 % in ferrite - but they distort the lattice and control the hardness of steel.

body.en:
Two metals do not dissolve in each other in every proportion. The four rules below say when a wide substitutional solution is possible; break one of them and the solubility drops, break several and the pair prefers to form a compound with a fixed composition. That compound - CuAl2, Fe3C, Mg2Si - is called an intermediate phase: it has its own lattice, its own melting point, and usually it is hard and brittle.

title.en: 2.4 Reading a binary phase diagram, and the lever rule
title.gu: 2.4 Binary phase diagram વાંચવું, અને lever rule

h.en: Copper-nickel: the isomorphous diagram and the lever rule
h.gu: Copper-nickel: isomorphous diagram અને lever rule

body.en:
Copper and nickel pass all the Hume-Rothery tests, so their diagram is the simplest one possible: a single liquidus above a single solidus, meeting at the melting points of the two pure metals. Every alloy of the pair begins to freeze at its liquidus, finishes at its solidus, and inside the lens between them two phases - liquid and solid solution - sit side by side. The compositions of those two phases are read at the two ends of a horizontal tie line drawn at the temperature of interest, and how much of each there is comes from the lever rule.

lever rule on a tie line at T, alloy composition C0: W(liquid) = (C_s - C0) / (C_s - C_l) W(solid) = (C0 - C_l) / (C_s - C_l) W(liquid) + W(solid) = 1 50 % Ni at 1300 C: C_l = 40 % Ni, C_s = 60 % Ni W(liquid) = (60 - 50)/(60 - 40) = 10/20 = 0.50 W(solid) = (50 - 40)/(60 - 40) = 10/20 = 0.50 in 2 kg of alloy: 1.00 kg liquid and 1.00 kg solid, of 40 % and 60 % Ni

Why it is true. The lever rule is a balance, not a formula to memorise: the amount of a phase is inversely proportional to its distance from the alloy composition, exactly like a see-saw. The phase whose composition is far from C0 must be present in small amount, which is why the answer for the 50 % alloy comes out equal - it sits exactly in the middle.

Check your answer. A quick check that catches most mistakes: at the liquidus, W(liquid) must be 1; at the solidus it must be 0. Put C0 = C_l and C0 = C_s in your own formula and see.

કેમ સાચું છે. Lever rule એ સંતુલન છે, યાદ રાખવાનું સૂત્ર નહીં: phase ની માત્રા alloy ના composition થી તેના અંતરની વ્યસ્ત પ્રમાણમાં હોય છે, જેમ સીસોડિયું. જે phase નું composition C0 થી દૂર હોય તેની માત્રા ઓછી જ હોય, અને તેથી જ 50 % alloy નો જવાબ સરખો આવે - તે બરાબર વચ્ચે બેસે છે.

જવાબ ચકાસો. મોટા ભાગની ભૂલ પકડતી ઝડપી ચકાસણી: liquidus પર W(liquid) = 1 થવું જોઈએ; solidus પર 0. તમારા સૂત્રમાં C0 = C_l અને C0 = C_s મૂકી જુઓ.

h.gu: Lead-tin: eutectic diagram અને તેનાં બિંદુઓ

body.en:
Lead and tin fail the size and structure tests, so each dissolves only a little of the other: at 183 C lead takes 19.2 % tin and tin takes 2.5 % lead. The two liquidus branches therefore meet at a single point - the eutectic point, 61.9 % tin and 183 C - where the liquid freezes all at once into the two solid solutions, α and β. An alloy of eutectic composition has no freezing range at all: it is liquid at 184 C and solid at 182 C, which is exactly what a solder or a type metal wants.

h.en: Iron changes its own lattice, and that is the whole subject
h.gu: Iron પોતાનું lattice બદલે છે, અને આખો વિષય એમાં જ છે

body.en:
Pure iron is allotropic: between 912 C and 1394 C it is FCC (austenite, γ), below 912 C and above 1394 C it is BCC (ferrite, α, and the high-temperature δ which is also BCC). The FCC lattice has a bigger hole in the middle, so austenite can hold 2.14 % carbon while ferrite holds only 0.02 %. That single fact explains the whole heat treatment of steel: heat it into the austenite range, the carbon dissolves; cool it slowly, the carbon comes back out as cementite; cool it fast, the carbon is trapped.

Why it is true. The line E-S (the Acm) and the line G-S (the A3) are the two boundaries a heat treater aims at. Heat a 0.4 % steel above A3 and it becomes all austenite; hold it there and the carbon is evenly spread; cool it and whatever you cool it into is the structure you get. Every heat treatment is a choice of temperature on this diagram and a choice of cooling rate off it.

Common mistake. Cementite is not a phase you can see as a metal - it is a compound, Fe3C, 6.67 % carbon, hard and brittle. Pearlite is not a third phase either: it is a two-phase mixture of ferrite and cementite, and it is called a micro-constituent, not a phase.

h.en: Heat treatment: three steps, one purpose
h.gu: Heat treatment: ત્રણ પગલાં, એક હેતુ

body.en:
Heat treatment is the controlled heating and cooling of a solid metal to change its structure, and through the structure its properties - without changing the shape of the part and without changing its composition. Every treatment has the same three steps: heat to a chosen temperature and hold it until the structure is uniform, then cool at a chosen rate. The temperature decides what structure you start from; the cooling rate decides what structure you finish with.

TreatmentHeat toCool byWhat it gives
Full annealing30-50 C above A3 (or A1 for hypereutectoid)furnace cooling, very slowsoft, coarse pearlite; easy to machine
Normalising30-50 C above A3still airfiner pearlite, higher strength than annealed
Hardening30-50 C above A3 or Acmquench in water, oil or brinemartensite: hardest, most brittle
Temperingbelow A1, 150-650 Cany, then air cooltoughness back; hardness set by the temperature
Case hardeningsurface only, with carbon or nitrogenquench after diffusinghard skin on a tough core
A1 = 727 C for every steel (the eutectoid line) A3 falls from 912 C at 0 % C to 727 C at 0.8 % C (hypoeutectoid steels) Acm rises from 727 C at 0.8 % C to 1147 C at 2.14 % C (hypereutectoid steels) so 0.4 % C steel is austenitised at about 800-830 C and 1.2 % C steel at about 750-780 C - above A1, below Acm

Why it is true. Hardening is not about the carbon alone: it is about how fast the austenite is cooled. Slow cooling gives the carbon time to diffuse out and form cementite; fast cooling does not, and the carbon is trapped in a strained lattice. That trapped structure, martensite, is hard because the carbon has nowhere to go - and it is brittle for the same reason, which is why it is always tempered.

Check your answer. The three steps answer three different questions: temperature decides which phase you begin with, holding time decides how even it is, cooling rate decides what you end with. An answer that mentions only temperature is half an answer.

Question (6 marks)

Apply the phase rule at four points and state what the number means: (a) pure iron at 1450 C in the austenite field, (b) pure iron at 1538 C where solid and liquid coexist, (c) the lead-tin eutectic at 183 C, (d) a 40 % tin alloy at 200 C where alpha and liquid coexist.

Step 1 - the formula and the components

F = C - P + 2, and at the fixed pressure of 1 atm we use F = C - P + 1 pure iron: C = 1 iron-carbon or lead-tin: C = 2

Step 2 - one point at a time

(a) C=1, P=1 (austenite only) F = 1-1+1 = 1 (b) C=1, P=2 (solid + liquid) F = 1-2+1 = 0 (c) C=2, P=3 (L + alpha + beta) F = 2-3+1 = 0 (d) C=2, P=2 (alpha + liquid) F = 2-2+1 = 1

Step 3 - what the numbers mean

F = 1: choose the temperature, the compositions then follow the field boundaries F = 0: nothing is free - the point is invariant at the melting point of iron the temperature stays at 1538 C until it is all liquid at 183 C the lead-tin eutectic freezes completely at that one temperature
(a) F = 1, (b) F = 0 invariant, (c) F = 0 invariant, (d) F = 1

Point (c) is the reason a eutectic alloy freezes at a single temperature: with three phases in a two-component system there is no freedom left, so the temperature cannot fall until one phase disappears. Point (d) is the ordinary two-phase field - you pick the temperature and the tie line then fixes both compositions, which is why the lever rule works there.

Check your answer. If you use F = C - P + 2 without fixing the pressure, every answer here goes up by one. Say which rule you are using - the examiner is looking for that sentence.

h.en: Lever rule on a lead-tin alloy

body.en:
Question (7 marks)

A 40 % tin solder is held at 200 C. Read the compositions of the two phases from the diagram, find the mass of each in 2 kg of alloy, and say what happens to the last liquid when the alloy cools to 183 C.

Step 1 - read the tie line

at 200 C the tie line runs from C_alpha to C_liquid alpha (lead-rich, left end): C_alpha = 17 % Sn liquid (right end): C_L = 55 % Sn alloy: C0 = 40 % Sn

Step 2 - the lever rule

W_L = (C0 - C_alpha)/(C_L - C_alpha) = (40 - 17)/(55 - 17) = 23/38 = 0.605 W_alpha = (C_L - C0)/(C_L - C_alpha) = (55 - 40)/(55 - 17) = 15/38 = 0.395 check: 0.605 + 0.395 = 1.000

Step 3 - the masses in 2 kg

m_L = 0.605 x 2 = 1.21 kg of liquid, 55 % Sn m_alpha = 0.395 x 2 = 0.79 kg of alpha, 17 % Sn the liquid is the phase farther from C0, so it is the larger one
17 % and 55 % Sn, 60.5 % liquid and 39.5 % alpha, 1.21 kg and 0.79 kg

As the alloy cools further the liquid follows the liquidus down to the eutectic point: the last drop of liquid is 61.9 % tin and it freezes at 183 C into alpha and beta together. That is why the microstructure of a 40 % solder shows primary alpha with eutectic between the arms.

Common mistake. The lever rule arms are measured from C0, not from zero: taking (40 - 0)/(55 - 17) is the commonest mistake and it gives an answer larger than 1.

Question (7 marks)

A 50 % nickel cupro-nickel is at 1300 C. Find the composition of the liquid and of the solid, the mass of each in 3 kg, and show that the same alloy at 1250 C is completely solid.

Step 1 - the tie line at 1300 C

liquidus at 1300 C: C_L = 40 % Ni solidus at 1300 C: C_s = 60 % Ni alloy: C0 = 50 % Ni

Step 2 - the lever rule and the masses

W_L = (60 - 50)/(60 - 40) = 0.50 W_s = (50 - 40)/(60 - 40) = 0.50 m_L = 1.50 kg, m_s = 1.50 kg in 3 kg of alloy

Step 3 - the check at 1250 C

solidus at 50 % Ni: interpolate between (40, 1240) and (60, 1300) T_solidus = 1240 + (50 - 40)/(60 - 40) x 60 = 1270 C 1250 C is below 1270 C, so the alloy has already finished freezing W_L = 0 - it is 100 % solid solution, 50 % Ni throughout
40 % and 60 % Ni, half and half (1.5 kg each), and at 1250 C it is 100 % solid

Why it is true. Both answers come from the same diagram, which is the point of drawing one. The tie line gives the compositions, the lever rule gives the amounts, and the boundary of the field tells you when an answer of zero must be expected.

Check your answer. A single-phase field always answers 100 % of one phase; if your lever rule gives a negative weight, the alloy is not in the two-phase field at all.

h.en: Pearlite and cementite in two steels

body.en:
Question (8 marks)

Using the eutectoid values, find the percentage of pearlite and of proeutectoid ferrite in a 0.4 % carbon steel, and the percentage of cementite in a 1.2 % carbon steel. Give the masses in 5 kg of each and explain the difference in properties.

Step 1 - the phase boundaries

ferrite at 727 C: 0.02 % C eutectoid austenite: 0.80 % C cementite: 6.67 % C

Step 2 - the 0.4 % steel

pearlite % = (0.40 - 0.02)/(0.80 - 0.02) x 100 = 0.38/0.78 x 100 = 48.7 % proeutectoid ferrite = 100 - 48.7 = 51.3 % in 5 kg: pearlite 2.44 kg, ferrite 2.56 kg

Step 3 - the 1.2 % steel

Fe3C % = (1.20 - 0.80)/(6.67 - 0.80) x 100 = 0.40/5.87 x 100 = 6.8 % pearlite = 100 - 6.8 = 93.2 % in 5 kg: cementite 0.34 kg, pearlite 4.66 kg
0.4 % C: 48.7 % pearlite; 1.2 % C: 6.8 % cementite; masses 2.44 / 0.34 kg

The 0.4 % steel is half soft ferrite, so it is tough and is used for shafts and axles. The 1.2 % steel has a cementite network round every grain, so it is much harder and much more brittle - the right choice for a file, the wrong one for a shaft.

Common mistake. Below 0.8 % carbon the formula for cementite gives a negative number - that is the signal that there is no proeutectoid cementite in the steel, not that the formula is wrong.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (8 marks)

Eutectoid મૂલ્યો વાપરીને 0.4 % carbon સ્ટીલમાં pearlite અને proeutectoid ferrite ની ટકાવારી, અને 1.2 % carbon સ્ટીલમાં cementite ની ટકાવારી શોધો. દરેકના 5 kg માં દળ આપો અને ગુણધર્મોમાં ફરક સમજાવો.

પગલું 1 - phase સીમાઓ

ferrite at 727 C: 0.02 % C eutectoid austenite: 0.80 % C cementite: 6.67 % C

પગલું 2 - 0.4 % સ્ટીલ

pearlite % = (0.40 - 0.02)/(0.80 - 0.02) x 100 = 0.38/0.78 x 100 = 48.7 % proeutectoid ferrite = 100 - 48.7 = 51.3 % in 5 kg: pearlite 2.44 kg, ferrite 2.56 kg

પગલું 3 - 1.2 % સ્ટીલ

Fe3C % = (1.20 - 0.80)/(6.67 - 0.80) x 100 = 0.40/5.87 x 100 = 6.8 % pearlite = 100 - 6.8 = 93.2 % in 5 kg: cementite 0.34 kg, pearlite 4.66 kg
0.4 % C: 48.7 % pearlite; 1.2 % C: 6.8 % cementite; masses 2.44 / 0.34 kg

0.4 % સ્ટીલ અડધું નરમ ferrite છે, તેથી તે tough છે અને shafts તથા axles માટે વપરાય. 1.2 % સ્ટીલમાં દરેક grain ફરતે cementite ની જાળી હોય છે, તેથી તે ઘણું સખત અને ઘણું ભંગુર છે - file માટે યોગ્ય, shaft માટે ખોટું.

સામાન્ય ભૂલ. 0.8 % થી નીચે carbon હોય તો cementite નું સૂત્ર ઋણ આંકડો આપે - એ સંકેત છે કે સ્ટીલમાં proeutectoid cementite નથી, સૂત્ર ખોટું નથી.

h.en: Hall-Petch: two grain sizes and a target strength
h.gu: Hall-Petch: બે grain size અને એક લક્ષ્ય તાકાત

body.en:
Question (6 marks)

For a low carbon steel sigma_0 = 100 MPa and k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5. Find the yield strength for grain sizes of 0.25 mm and 0.04 mm, and the grain size needed for a yield strength of 300 MPa.

Step 1 - the relation

sigma_y = sigma_0 + k d^(-1/2) d must be in mm, otherwise k has a different value

Step 2 - the two grain sizes

d = 0.25 mm: d^-1/2 = 1/0.5 = 2.00 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 2.00 = 147 MPa d = 0.04 mm: d^-1/2 = 1/0.2 = 5.00 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 5.00 = 217 MPa the finer grain is 70 MPa stronger, with the same composition

Step 3 - the grain size for 300 MPa

300 = 100 + 23.4 d^(-1/2) d^(-1/2) = 200/23.4 = 8.547 d = 1/8.547^2 = 0.0137 mm = 13.7 micrometre
147 MPa, 217 MPa, and d = 0.0137 mm for 300 MPa

Why it is true. The 13.7 micrometre grain is fine but not impossible: normalising a 0.2 % steel gives about 20 micrometre and a controlled rolling schedule reaches 10. The limit is that very fine grains coarsen when the steel is welded or held hot.

Check your answer. Put the answers back: 100 + 23.4/0.5 = 147 and 100 + 23.4/0.2 = 217, and for the third 100 + 23.4 x 8.547 = 300. All three close.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (6 marks)

ઓછા carbon ના સ્ટીલ માટે sigma_0 = 100 MPa અને k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5 છે. 0.25 mm અને 0.04 mm grain size માટે yield strength શોધો, અને 300 MPa yield strength માટે જરૂરી grain size શોધો.

પગલું 1 - સંબંધ

sigma_y = sigma_0 + k d^(-1/2) d must be in mm, otherwise k has a different value

પગલું 2 - બે grain size

d = 0.25 mm: d^-1/2 = 1/0.5 = 2.00 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 2.00 = 147 MPa d = 0.04 mm: d^-1/2 = 1/0.2 = 5.00 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 5.00 = 217 MPa the finer grain is 70 MPa stronger, with the same composition

પગલું 3 - 300 MPa માટે grain size

300 = 100 + 23.4 d^(-1/2) d^(-1/2) = 200/23.4 = 8.547 d = 1/8.547^2 = 0.0137 mm = 13.7 micrometre
147 MPa, 217 MPa, and d = 0.0137 mm for 300 MPa

કેમ સાચું છે. 13.7 micrometre નું grain નાનું છે પણ અશક્ય નહીં: 0.2 % સ્ટીલ normalise કરો તો લગભગ 20 micrometre મળે અને નિયંત્રિત rolling થી 10 સુધી પહોંચાય. મર્યાદા એ છે કે ખૂબ નાના grains વેલ્ડિંગ કે ગરમ રાખવાથી જાડા થઈ જાય.

જવાબ ચકાસો. જવાબ પાછા મૂકો: 100 + 23.4/0.5 = 147 અને 100 + 23.4/0.2 = 217, અને ત્રીજા માટે 100 + 23.4 x 8.547 = 300. ત્રણેય મળે છે.

h.en: From an ASTM grain size number to a yield strength
h.gu: ASTM grain size number થી yield strength સુધી

body.en:
Question (7 marks)

A micrograph of a steel shows ASTM grain size 6, another shows 10. Convert both to a grain diameter in millimetres and then to a yield strength with sigma_0 = 100 MPa and k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5, and state the percentage gain.

Step 1 - the ASTM number to a grain diameter

d = 25.4/(100 x sqrt(2^(N-1))) mm N = 6: n = 2^5 = 32, d = 25.4/(100 x 5.657) = 0.0449 mm N = 10: n = 2^9 = 512, d = 25.4/(100 x 22.63) = 0.0112 mm

Step 2 - Hall-Petch for each

N = 6: d^-1/2 = 1/sqrt(0.0449) = 4.72 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 4.72 = 210 MPa N = 10: d^-1/2 = 1/sqrt(0.0112) = 9.45 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 9.45 = 321 MPa

Step 3 - the gain

gain = (321 - 210)/210 x 100 = 52.9 % for four ASTM numbers, about 53 % more yield strength
0.045 mm and 0.011 mm; 210 MPa and 321 MPa; a 53 % gain

Four ASTM numbers is a factor of four in grain size, which is a factor of two in d^-1/2 - and that is why the gain is not 400 % but 53 %. Hall-Petch is linear in d^-1/2, not in d.

Common mistake. d must be in millimetres for this k. Feed the value in micrometres and the answer comes out about thirty times too large.
body.gu:
પ્રશ્ન (7 marks)

એક સ્ટીલના micrograph માં ASTM grain size 6 છે, બીજામાં 10. બંનેને મિલીમીટરમાં grain diameter અને પછી sigma_0 = 100 MPa તથા k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5 સાથે yield strength માં ફેરવો, અને ટકાવારી વધારો કહો.

પગલું 1 - ASTM number થી grain diameter

d = 25.4/(100 x sqrt(2^(N-1))) mm N = 6: n = 2^5 = 32, d = 25.4/(100 x 5.657) = 0.0449 mm N = 10: n = 2^9 = 512, d = 25.4/(100 x 22.63) = 0.0112 mm

પગલું 2 - દરેક માટે Hall-Petch

N = 6: d^-1/2 = 1/sqrt(0.0449) = 4.72 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 4.72 = 210 MPa N = 10: d^-1/2 = 1/sqrt(0.0112) = 9.45 -> sigma_y = 100 + 23.4 x 9.45 = 321 MPa

પગલું 3 - વધારો

gain = (321 - 210)/210 x 100 = 52.9 % for four ASTM numbers, about 53 % more yield strength
0.045 mm and 0.011 mm; 210 MPa and 321 MPa; a 53 % gain

ચાર ASTM number એ grain size માં ચાર ગણો ફરક છે, જે d^-1/2 માં બે ગણો ફરક છે - અને તેથી જ વધારો 400 % નહીં પણ 53 % છે. Hall-Petch d^-1/2 માં રેખીય છે, d માં નહીં.

સામાન્ય ભૂલ. આ k માટે d મિલીમીટરમાં જ જોઈએ. Micrometre માં મૂકો તો જવાબ લગભગ ત્રીસ ગણો મોટો આવે.

title.en: Cooling curves of a pure metal and an alloy
title.gu: શુદ્ધ ધાતુ અને alloy ની cooling curve

caption.en: A pure metal freezes at one temperature and the curve stays flat while the latent heat comes out; an alloy freezes over a range between its liquidus and solidus, so the curve only changes slope.
caption.gu: શુદ્ધ ધાતુ એક જ temperature પર થીજે અને latent heat નીકળે ત્યાં સુધી રેખા સપાટ રહે; alloy liquidus અને solidus વચ્ચેની range માં થીજે તેથી રેખા ફક્ત ઢાળ બદલે.

title.en: Grain structure of a cast ingot

caption.en: The mould wall chills the metal first, so fine equiaxed grains form there, columnar grains grow inwards along the heat flow, and the hot centre freezes last as coarse equiaxed grains.
caption.gu: Mould ની દીવાલ પહેલી ઠંડી થાય તેથી ત્યાં નાના grains બને, ગરમીના પ્રવાહ સાથે અંદર તરફ લાંબા columnar grains વધે, અને ગરમ વચ્ચે છેલ્લે જાડા equiaxed grains થીજે.

caption.en: A substitutional solution swaps one atom for another of similar size (Cu-Ni); an interstitial solution hides a small atom in the gaps (carbon in iron) - which is why carbon fits in iron only up to 2.14 %.
caption.gu: Substitutional solution માં સરખા માપનો atom બીજાની જગ્યાએ બેસે (Cu-Ni); interstitial solution માં નાનો atom ખાલી જગ્યામાં બેસે (iron માં carbon) - તેથી જ carbon iron માં 2.14 % સુધી જ બેસે.

caption.en: Copper and nickel dissolve in each other in every proportion, so the diagram has no eutectic: one liquidus above one solidus, and a tie line that gives both phases.
caption.gu: Copper અને nickel દરેક પ્રમાણમાં એકબીજામાં ઓગળે, તેથી diagram માં eutectic નથી: એક liquidus નીચે એક solidus, અને tie line બંને phase આપે.

caption.en: Lead and tin barely dissolve in each other, so the two liquidus branches meet at the eutectic 183 C and 61.9 % tin, where the alloy freezes at a single temperature.
caption.gu: Lead અને tin એકબીજામાં થોડા જ ઓગળે, તેથી બંને liquidus શાખા eutectic પર મળે - 183 C અને 61.9 % tin - જ્યાં alloy એક જ temperature પર થીજે.

title.gu: Iron-iron carbide diagram ના મુખ્ય બિંદુઓ

caption.en: Carbon up to 2.14 % dissolves in austenite; at 0.8 % and 727 C that austenite turns into pearlite, the eutectoid reaction that every heat treatment of steel works around.
caption.gu: Austenite માં carbon 2.14 % સુધી ઓગળે; 0.8 % અને 727 C પર એ austenite pearlite બને, અને સ્ટીલની દરેક heat treatment એ જ eutectoid ફરતે ફરે છે.

caption.en: Below 0.8 % carbon the pearlite sits in a field of ferrite, at 0.8 % it fills the micrograph, and above 0.8 % cementite appears on the grain boundaries as a brittle network.
caption.gu: 0.8 % થી નીચે pearlite ferrite ના ખેતરમાં દેખાય, બરાબર 0.8 % પર આખું micrograph pearlite હોય, અને 0.8 % થી ઉપર cementite grain boundary પર ભંગુર જાળી બનાવે.

title.en: Grain size sets the yield strength
title.gu: Grain size yield strength નક્કી કરે છે

caption.en: Yield strength rises with the square root of the reciprocal grain size: halving the grain size raises the strength by about 40 % for the same steel.
caption.gu: Yield strength grain size ના વ્યસ્ત વર્ગમૂળ સાથે વધે: grain size અડધું કરો તો એ જ સ્ટીલની તાકાત લગભગ 40 % વધે.

title.en: Phase rule and the lever rule

items.f: F = C - P + 2   (F = C - P + 1 at fixed pressure)

terms.en: F degrees of freedom, C components, P phases. F = 0 means an invariant point.
terms.gu: F degrees of freedom, C components, P phases. F = 0 એટલે invariant બિંદુ.

terms.en: Compositions read at the two ends of the tie line at that temperature.
terms.gu: તે temperature પરની tie line ના બે છેડે composition વંચાય છે.

terms.en: The phase farther from C0 is present in smaller amount.
terms.gu: C0 થી દૂરનો phase ઓછી માત્રામાં હોય છે.

terms.en: Use it on every lever-rule answer before writing the final line.
terms.gu: દરેક lever-rule જવાબમાં અંતિમ લીટી પહેલાં આ વાપરો.

terms.en: gamma surface energy, L latent heat per volume, dT undercooling.
terms.gu: gamma surface energy, L volume દીઠ latent heat, dT undercooling.

items.f: dG* = 16 pi gamma^3 Tm^2/(3 L^2 dT^2)

terms.en: Falls as 1/dT^2, so a little more undercooling gives many more nuclei.
terms.gu: 1/dT^2 જેટલું ઘટે, તેથી થોડું વધુ undercooling ઘણા વધુ nuclei આપે.

terms.en: m mass of metal, q the rate at which the mould removes heat.
terms.gu: m ધાતુનું દળ, q એ mould ગરમી લે તેવો દર.

terms.en: The mushy zone where liquid and solid coexist.
terms.gu: Mushy zone જ્યાં પ્રવાહી અને ઘન સાથે રહે.

terms.en: d in mm gives k in MPa mm^0.5; 100 and 23.4 for the steel of this unit.
terms.gu: d mm માં હોય તો k MPa mm^0.5 માં; આ unit ના સ્ટીલ માટે 100 અને 23.4.

terms.en: n is the number of grains per square inch at 100 magnification.
terms.gu: n એ 100 magnification પર પ્રતિ ચોરસ ઇંચ grains ની સંખ્યા છે.

terms.en: The 3.32 is 1/log10(2); count three fields and average.
terms.gu: 3.32 એ 1/log10(2) છે; ત્રણ જગ્યાએ ગણીને સરેરાશ લો.

terms.en: N = 6 gives 0.045 mm and N = 10 gives 0.011 mm.
Lever rule between the ferrite limit 0.02 and the eutectoid 0.80.
terms.gu: Ferrite મર્યાદા 0.02 અને eutectoid 0.80 વચ્ચેનો lever rule.

terms.en: Only for hypereutectoid steels; below 0.8 % it gives a negative number.
terms.gu: ફક્ત hypereutectoid સ્ટીલ માટે; 0.8 % ની નીચે તે ઋણ આંકડો આપે.

items.f: eutectic: L(4.3) -> gamma + Fe3C at 1147;  eutectoid: gamma(0.8) -> alpha + Fe3C at 727

terms.en: The first makes ledeburite in cast iron, the second makes pearlite in steel.
terms.gu: પહેલી cast iron માં ledeburite બનાવે, બીજી સ્ટીલમાં pearlite.

terms.en: The same for every steel; nothing transforms below it except tempering.
terms.gu: દરેક સ્ટીલ માટે એ જ; તેની નીચે tempering સિવાય કંઈ બદલાતું નથી.

terms.en: An approximation of the G-S line, good to about 10 C up to 0.8 % C.
terms.gu: G-S રેખાનો અંદાજ, 0.8 % C સુધી લગભગ 10 C સુધી સાચો.

terms.en: The S-E line; hardening temperature is kept just above A1 for these steels.
terms.gu: S-E રેખા; આ સ્ટીલ માટે hardening temperature A1 થી થોડું ઉપર રખાય.

q.en: What is a phase, and how many phases are in a 0.4 % carbon steel at room temperature?
q.gu: Phase એટલે શું, અને room temperature પર 0.4 % carbon સ્ટીલમાં કેટલા phase છે?

a.en: A part of the material with the same structure and composition everywhere. Two: ferrite and cementite, arranged as ferrite grains and pearlite.
a.gu: સામગ્રીનો જે ભાગ બધે એક જ રચના અને composition ધરાવે. બે: ferrite અને cementite, જે ferrite grains અને pearlite સ્વરૂપે ગોઠવાયેલા છે.

q.en: State the Gibbs phase rule and give one invariant point from this unit.
q.gu: Gibbs phase rule કહો અને આ unit માંથી એક invariant બિંદુ આપો.

a.en: F = C - P + 2, and F = C - P + 1 once the pressure is fixed at one atmosphere. The lead-tin eutectic at 183 C and 61.9 % tin has C = 2 P = 3, so F = 0 - an invariant point.
a.gu: F = C - P + 2, અને pressure એક જ atmosphere પર નિશ્ચિત હોય તો F = C - P + 1. 183 C અને 61.9 % tin પરનું lead-tin eutectic માં C = 2, P = 3, તેથી F = 0 - invariant બિંદુ.

q.en: Why does a pure metal show a flat arrest on its cooling curve but an alloy does not?
q.gu: શુદ્ધ ધાતુની cooling curve સપાટ arrest કેમ દેખાય પણ alloy માં નહીં?

a.en: A pure metal freezes at one temperature, so the latent heat holds the curve flat. An alloy freezes over a range, releasing latent heat gradually, so only the slope changes.
a.gu: શુદ્ધ ધાતુ એક જ temperature પર થીજે તેથી latent heat રેખા સપાટ રાખે. Alloy એક range માં થીજે અને latent heat ધીમે છોડે, તેથી ફક્ત ઢાળ બદલાય.

q.gu: Hume-Rothery ના કોઈ પણ ત્રણ નિયમ કહો.

a.en: Size difference below 15 %; the same crystal structure; similar valency and electronegativity. Break them and solubility falls or a compound forms.
a.gu: માપનો ફરક 15 % થી ઓછો; એક જ crystal structure; સરખી valency અને electronegativity. તૂટે તો solubility ઘટે કે compound બને.

q.en: Why is carbon interstitial in iron while nickel is substitutional?
q.gu: Iron માં carbon interstitial અને nickel substitutional કેમ છે?

a.en: Carbon's radius is 77 pm against iron's 126 pm, far too small for a lattice site, so it sits in the gaps. Nickel is 125 pm, almost exactly iron's size.
a.gu: Carbon ની radius 77 pm છે જ્યારે iron ની 126 pm, lattice ની જગ્યા માટે ઘણી નાની, તેથી તે ખાલી જગ્યામાં બેસે. Nickel 125 pm છે, લગભગ iron જેટલી જ.

q.en: Read out the compositions of the two phases at 1300 C in the Cu-Ni diagram.
q.gu: Cu-Ni diagram માં 1300 C પર બે phase નું composition કહો.

a.en: 40 % nickel in the liquid and 60 % nickel in the solid, from the two ends of the tie line, and the lever rule then gives half of each for a 50 % alloy.
a.gu: Tie line ના બે છેડે પ્રવાહીમાં 40 % nickel અને ઘનમાં 60 % nickel, અને પછી lever rule 50 % alloy માટે દરેકનો અડધો ભાગ આપે.

q.en: What is the difference between the eutectic and the eutectoid of the Fe-C diagram?
q.gu: Fe-C diagram ના eutectic અને eutectoid માં શું ફરક છે?

a.en: The eutectic at 1147 C and 4.3 % C turns liquid into two solids. The eutectoid at 727 C and 0.8 % C turns one solid (austenite) into two solids (ferrite and cementite).
a.gu: 1147 C અને 4.3 % C પરનું eutectic પ્રવાહીને બે ઘનમાં ફેરવે. 727 C અને 0.8 % C પરનું eutectoid એક ઘન (austenite) ને બે ઘન (ferrite અને cementite) માં ફેરવે.

q.en: Why can austenite hold 2.14 % carbon but ferrite only 0.02 %?
q.gu: Austenite 2.14 % carbon કેમ રાખી શકે પણ ferrite ફક્ત 0.02 %?

a.en: Austenite is FCC and its interstitial hole is larger and there are more of them per cell; ferrite is BCC with a smaller, distorted hole.
a.gu: Austenite FCC છે અને તેની interstitial જગ્યા મોટી તથા cell દીઠ વધુ છે; ferrite BCC છે જેની જગ્યા નાની અને વળેલી છે.

q.en: What happens to the microstructure of a 1.2 % carbon steel cooled slowly?
q.gu: 1.2 % carbon સ્ટીલને ધીમે ઠંડું કરો તો microstructure શું થાય?

a.en: Proeutectoid cementite forms a network on the austenite grain boundaries and the rest becomes pearlite - about 6.8 % cementite and 93 % pearlite.
a.gu: Proeutectoid cementite austenite grain boundary પર જાળી બનાવે અને બાકીનું pearlite થાય - લગભગ 6.8 % cementite અને 93 % pearlite.

q.en: What are the three steps of any heat treatment?
q.gu: કોઈ પણ heat treatment નાં ત્રણ પગલાં કયાં છે?

a.en: Heat to a chosen temperature above the critical line, hold until the structure is uniform, and cool at a chosen rate.
a.gu: Critical line ઉપર પસંદ કરેલા temperature સુધી ગરમ કરવું, રચના સરખી થાય ત્યાં સુધી રાખવું, અને પસંદ કરેલા દરથી ઠંડું કરવું.

q.en: What is the difference between annealing and normalising?
q.gu: Annealing અને normalising માં શું ફરક છે?

a.en: The temperature is the same; the cooling is different. Annealing cools in the furnace and gives soft coarse pearlite, normalising cools in air and gives finer, stronger pearlite.
a.gu: Temperature એ જ છે; ઠંડું કરવાની રીત જુદી છે. Annealing furnace માં ઠંડું કરે અને નરમ જાડું pearlite આપે, normalising હવામાં ઠંડું કરે અને નાનું, વધુ મજબૂત pearlite આપે.

q.en: Why is a hardened steel always tempered?
q.gu: Hardened સ્ટીલને હંમેશા temper કેમ કરાય છે?

a.en: Quenching traps carbon and leaves martensite, which is very hard but brittle. Tempering below A1 relieves the strain and restores toughness at some cost in hardness.
a.gu: Quenching carbon ફસાવે અને martensite રહે, જે ખૂબ સખત પણ ભંગુર છે. A1 ની નીચે tempering તણાવ ઘટાડે અને hardness થોડી ગુમાવીને toughness પાછી આપે.

q.en: Apply the phase rule at four points and state what the number means: (a) pure iron at 1450 C in the austenite field, (b) pure iron at 1538 C where solid and liquid coexist, (c) the lead-tin eutectic at 183 C, (d) a 40 % tin alloy at 200 C where alpha and liquid coexist.
q.gu: ચાર બિંદુ પર phase rule લાગુ કરો અને આંકડાનો અર્થ કહો: (a) austenite વિસ્તારમાં 1450 C પર શુદ્ધ iron, (b) 1538 C પર જ્યાં ઘન અને પ્રવાહી સાથે છે, (c) 183 C પરનું lead-tin eutectic, (d) 200 C પર 40 % tin નું alloy જ્યાં alpha અને પ્રવાહી સાથે છે.

q.en: A 40 % tin solder is held at 200 C. Read the compositions of the two phases from the diagram, find the mass of each in 2 kg of alloy, and say what happens to the last liquid when the alloy cools to 183 C.
q.gu: 40 % tin નું solder 200 C પર રખાય છે. Diagram પરથી બે phase નું composition વાંચો, 2 kg alloy માં દરેકનું દળ શોધો, અને alloy 183 C સુધી ઠંડું થાય ત્યારે છેલ્લા પ્રવાહીનું શું થાય તે કહો.

q.en: A 50 % nickel cupro-nickel is at 1300 C. Find the composition of the liquid and of the solid, the mass of each in 3 kg, and show that the same alloy at 1250 C is completely solid.
q.gu: 50 % nickel નું cupro-nickel 1300 C પર છે. પ્રવાહી અને ઘનનું composition, 3 kg માં દરેકનું દળ શોધો, અને એ જ alloy 1250 C પર સંપૂર્ણ ઘન છે તે દર્શાવો.

q.en: Using the eutectoid values, find the percentage of pearlite and of proeutectoid ferrite in a 0.4 % carbon steel, and the percentage of cementite in a 1.2 % carbon steel. Give the masses in 5 kg of each and explain the difference in properties.
q.gu: Eutectoid મૂલ્યો વાપરીને 0.4 % carbon સ્ટીલમાં pearlite અને proeutectoid ferrite ની ટકાવારી, અને 1.2 % carbon સ્ટીલમાં cementite ની ટકાવારી શોધો. દરેકના 5 kg માં દળ આપો અને ગુણધર્મોમાં ફરક સમજાવો.

q.en: For a low carbon steel sigma_0 = 100 MPa and k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5. Find the yield strength for grain sizes of 0.25 mm and 0.04 mm, and the grain size needed for a yield strength of 300 MPa.
q.gu: ઓછા carbon ના સ્ટીલ માટે sigma_0 = 100 MPa અને k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5 છે. 0.25 mm અને 0.04 mm grain size માટે yield strength શોધો, અને 300 MPa yield strength માટે જરૂરી grain size શોધો.

q.en: A micrograph of a steel shows ASTM grain size 6, another shows 10. Convert both to a grain diameter in millimetres and then to a yield strength with sigma_0 = 100 MPa and k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5, and state the percentage gain.
q.gu: એક સ્ટીલના micrograph માં ASTM grain size 6 છે, બીજામાં 10. બંનેને મિલીમીટરમાં grain diameter અને પછી sigma_0 = 100 MPa તથા k = 23.4 MPa mm^0.5 સાથે yield strength માં ફેરવો, અને ટકાવારી વધારો કહો.
